name: Lin Zhenfu
current_role: Listed as co-holder of Lin family stake in Sichuan Kexin Mechanical and Electrical Equipment (SZSE: 300092); current role unconfirmed
profile: Appeared on Hurun China 2010 alongside Lin Zhenhua and Lin Zhenrong as a shared Lin family fortune from Sichuan Kexin, a Shifang, Sichuan maker of pressure vessels (incl. nuclear-grade equipment) founded 1997 and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2010. Lin Zhenhua is chairman; no public source found naming Lin Zhenfu's own role.
interesting_fact: Sichuan Kexin is one of the few Chinese makers of nuclear-grade pressure vessel equipment.
notes: Could not find any source (English or Chinese search) naming 林祯富 individually; wealth was a shared family listing with chairman Lin Zhenhua. Best route is via the company's Shenzhen-listed IR channels / chairman Lin Zhenhua. Low priority.

name: Vikram S Shriram
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd (since Sept 2001)
profile: Member of the Shriram business family, Vikram S. Shriram co-runs DCM Shriram, a Delhi-based conglomerate in chlor-alkali/vinyl chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, agri-inputs and captive power, alongside elder brother and Chairman Ajay S. Shriram. A chartered accountant, he has been Vice Chairman & MD since 2001.
interesting_fact: He is a qualified chartered accountant (Associate Member, ICAI) with a B.Com (Hons) from Calcutta University, and the company bio notes his strong aptitude for finance.
deep_cut_fact: After training across SRF Group functions, he joined Shriram Bearings Ltd in Ranchi in 1981 as senior management (works, marketing, general management); he studied at Mayo College, Ajmer, and lists swimming and cooking as hobbies.
notes: response@dcmshriram.com is the general corporate email in 2022-24 annual reports; shares@ appears in a 2022 AGM notice (shareholder services). DCM Shriram has a large captive power business - an angle for an energy podcast. Not to be confused with DCM Shriram Industries (separate company).

name: Chigurupati Krishna Prasad
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Granules India Ltd
profile: Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati founded Triton Laboratories in Hyderabad in 1984 with Uma Chigurupati to make paracetamol API; it grew into Granules India, among the world's largest makers of paracetamol, metformin and ibuprofen and a pioneer of pharmaceutical formulation intermediates (PFIs). He still leads it as CMD, pushing green-chemistry projects and a 2025 move into peptides.
interesting_fact: Granules commissioned what it called the world's largest single-site PFI plant at Gagillapur in 2003; he received the Economic Times Lifetime Achievement Award (2022) and an IOD Distinguished Fellowship (2025).
deep_cut_fact: In 1987 his first company, Triton Laboratories, became only the second Indian pharma company to export to the United States; Triton also pioneered selling bulk 'direct compressible' granulated paracetamol (PFIs).
notes: Granules' 'Healthy People, Healthy Planet' green-molecules push (Granules CZRO subsidiary) is a good sustainability/energy hook. Family also active in company (Uma, Priyanka, Harsha Chigurupati are EDs).

name: Wang Mingjun
current_role: Co-founder of the Boton flavours & fragrances group (China Boton Group, HKEX: 3318); chairman at 2005 IPO, current role unconfirmed
profile: Wang Mingjun (王明均) co-founded Shenzhen Boton Flavors & Fragrances in 1991 with his brothers Wang Mingfan, Wang Mingqing and Wang Mingyou; the group listed in Hong Kong in 2005 as China Flavors and Fragrances (now China Boton Group), with him as chairman. Brother Wang Mingfan is shown as Chairman & CEO in recent (2023) filings.
interesting_fact: The Boton group researches, makes and sells flavours and fragrances in China, mostly under the 'Boton' (波頓) brand, and was listed in Hong Kong in 2005 as China Flavors and Fragrances.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2005 Hong Kong prospectus, he joined the family venture in March 1991 and by IPO had ~20 years in flavour-and-fragrance management; the group was run by four Wang brothers.
notes: Sources conflict on who chairs China Boton today (one aggregator says Wang Mingjun chairman since 2012; 2023 pay records list brother Wang Mingfan as Chairman & CEO). Verify against latest HKEX annual report for 3318 before outreach. No published personal/office contact found.

name: Balram Garg
current_role: Managing Director, PC Jeweller Ltd (reappointed for five years, Aug 2026)
profile: Balram Garg co-founded PC Jeweller with his elder brother Padam Chand Gupta, coming from a wholesale gold-trading background; it opened its first showroom in Karol Bagh, Delhi in April 2005 and listed on NSE/BSE in December 2012. As MD he is leading a turnaround, converting promoter warrants into equity and raising promoter holding to ~39% in 2026.
interesting_fact: PC Jeweller went from a single Karol Bagh showroom in 2005 to 41 stores by March 2014 and listed after an oversubscribed 2012 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: The company was originally incorporated as 'P Chand Jewellers'; its Noida SEZ export unit won Highest Exporter and Best Exporter (gems & jewellery) awards for 2009-10 and 2010-11.
notes: Company went through a debt restructuring with lenders in recent years - avoid that topic. Corporate office is in Karol Bagh, New Delhi.

name: Rup Chand Lohia
current_role: Senior patriarch/director of the Merino Group (Merino Industries / Merino Panel Products, Kolkata); reportedly redesignated Chairman Emeritus in 2024
profile: Rup Chand Lohia is a senior member of the Lohia family behind the Kolkata-based Merino Group, one of India's largest makers of high-pressure decorative laminates, plus plywood, panels and food processing. The family business dates to 1965 (Hapur, UP); day-to-day leadership now sits with family members such as MD Prakash Lohia and CEO Manoj Lohia.
interesting_fact: Merino set up its first high-pressure decorative laminate plant at Hapur in 1981 and now runs laminate plants in Hapur, Rohad, Dahej and Hosur, among India's largest capacities.
notes: Very low public profile; Merino Industries is unlisted (CIN U51909WB1965PLC026556). 'Chairman Emeritus' (2024) came from a search summary of an annual report not directly verified. Best route is via Merino corporate office in Kolkata or MD Prakash Lohia. Alive status not confirmed (no obituary found).

name: Sevantilal Shah
current_role: Co-founder, Venus Jewel (Surat/Mumbai diamond manufacturer); trustee of Rasilaben Sevantilal Shah Venus Hospital, Surat
profile: Sevantilal Premchand Shah co-founded Venus Jewel in 1969 with elder brother Ramniklal; it became one of India's most respected diamond cutters and the first Indian firm to cut and polish 2-carat-plus stones at scale. The next generation (Anil, Rajesh, Hitesh) now runs the business while he focuses on philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Venus Jewel switched to cash-only terms when most Indian firms sold on 120-day-plus credit - a risky move that briefly dented sales until buyers came back for its cutting quality.
deep_cut_fact: After seeing patients' struggles during family hospital visits in 2016, he envisioned 'a hospital that runs on ethical grounds'; Venus Jewel put ~$6M into the Smt Rasilaben Sevantilal Shah Venus Hospital in Surat, opened in 2019 with PM Modi attending; ~70 Venus staff help run it.
notes: Received GJEPC Lifetime Achievement Award (March 2017). Elderly; alive status not confirmed but no obituary found. Country field empty in input - he is Indian (Surat). Best route likely via Venus Jewel / nephew Hitesh Shah. No published contact verified (company site unreachable).

name: Thomas J. Healy
profile: Thomas Healy founded Hyliion in 2015 out of Carnegie Mellon to electrify long-haul trucks and took it public via SPAC in Oct 2020 at a $1B+ valuation. After exiting the EV powertrain business in 2023, he pivoted Hyliion to the KARNO generator - a 3D-printed, fuel-agnostic linear-heat generator (tech bought from GE for $37M) pitched for data centers, the US Navy and oilfield power.
interesting_fact: He argues 'every electron will end up in a data center' and that providers now start site planning with 'How do we secure power?' rather than 'Where do we put servers?' - a direct fit for an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: A CMU mechanical engineering & public policy grad (ENG 2014, MS 2016) with a passion for racing and motorsports, he founded two startups while still in college before Hyliion; CMU honoured him as a 'Tartan on the Rise' and he sits on CMU's Board of Trustees.
notes: Top-priority guest for the podcast: young founder now selling on-site generators to data centers (Flexnode LOI for up to 10 KARNO units, US Navy and Air Force contracts). Does media readily (FreightWaves, Startup Junkie podcast). Forbes 30 Under 30 (2017).
